A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Q-DCP and H-DCP research. Their main text, equations, figures, proofs, and experimental appendices are readable and support comparison. The algorithms in v1 Appendix C are relocated into v2's main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR100 experiments on coverage, prediction-set size, communication costs, convergence, and hyperparameter sensitivity in Section 6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds federated-baseline comparisons, larger-network and sensitivity experiments, and PathMNIST results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Q-DCP retains its smoothed, regularized quantile loss, ADMM updates, averaging, and threshold correction. H-DCP retains its quantization, histogram consensus, and coverage correction. Algorithms 1–2 are relocated from Appendix C without procedural changes.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates CIFAR100 classification only. v2 adds nine-class PathMNIST medical-image classification in Appendix B.6 and Figures 16–17, substantially broadening the evaluated domain while retaining CIFAR100.

E2.justification: v1's empirical comparisons use centralized CP; FCP, FedCP-QQ, and WFCP appear as background methods. v2 Table 1 adds evaluated FCP and FedCP-QQ comparisons on a CIFAR100 star topology, with WFCP represented by the combined H-DCP(WFCP) column.

E3.justification: The original Section 6 settings remain. New protocols include 100-device experiments with 3000 iterations and varying network size and epsilon_0 on Erdős–Rényi graphs. PathMNIST uses eight devices, Q-DCP with 8000 iterations, and H-DCP with 80 iterations and 100 quantization levels to match communication costs.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds substantial scalability and sensitivity analyses: 100-device tests and experiments examining how network size interacts with epsilon_0 and coverage. Figures 10–11 expose undercoverage with epsilon_0 = 0.1 as the network grows. Existing convergence and smoothing, regularization, and quantization ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports averages over 10 randomly generated calibration sets without plotted variability. v2 adds uncertainty bands to Figures 2–5 and standard deviations in Table 1. Figure 2 identifies its bands as intervals covering 95% of realized values. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting; no increase in repetitions is stated.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports coverage/set-size pairs of 0.913/11.35 for Q-DCP, 0.920/12.16 for H-DCP(WFCP), 0.918/11.98 for FCP, and 0.996/45.32 for FedCP-QQ. Figures 8–11 and 16–17 add larger-network, network-size sensitivity, and PathMNIST findings. These expand the reported evidence rather than establish performance improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The assumptions, propositions, coverage theorems, bounds, and Appendix A proofs retain their mathematical substance. Changes such as Z_i to S_i in Equation 8 and p to x in Equation 34 correct notation without changing the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same two decentralized CP protocols, coverage claims, and trade-off between Q-DCP's tuning requirements and H-DCP's communication overhead. The added experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains that suitable epsilon_0 selection depends on network size and interprets the resulting coverage failures in Appendix B.3. It also motivates the torus experiment through intermediate connectivity, discusses medical applicability, and adds asynchronous networks as future work. These refine the existing interpretation and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-release repository address in the abstract. Appendix B.6 documents the PathMNIST split sizes, small-resnet14 shared model, device allocation, and communication settings. Existing algorithm descriptions and CIFAR100 implementation disclosures largely remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on Bayesian conformal prediction, federated learning, and asynchronous optimization, including Clarte and Zdeborova, McMahan et al., Kairouz et al., Wei and Ozdaglar, and Tian et al. The central research positioning remains; several other reference changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized explanations, notation corrections, affiliation and publication text updates, expanded Appendix B organization, and relocation of the algorithm descriptions from Appendix C into Sections 4–5.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 1 and six experimental figures, redraws main plots with uncertainty bands, and relocates the algorithm tables into the two-column main text. The original ablation Figures 8–11 remain as Figures 12–15. These substantially expand and reorganize the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation beyond v1's 20-device CIFAR100 study against centralized CP. Table 1 addresses the missing evaluated federated baselines, while Appendices B.3 and B.6 test scalability and a medical domain. Added uncertainty reporting and the network-dependent coverage failure analysis make reliability and practical limitations easier to assess, supporting a substantial overall quality improvement.
